principles.name: Capabilities reflect what the business does, not how it is organised
principles.statement: Business capabilities are defined by the outcomes the business produces, independent of the organisational unit that delivers them
principles.rationale: Org structures change frequently; the underlying capabilities are stable and provide a durable basis for investment decisions
implications: BUS-CAP is owned by the architecture function, not by org-design
Reorganisations do not change the capability map; they re-allocate ownership of existing capabilities
Process and application investments are mapped to capabilities first

principles.name: Outcome over output
principles.statement: Teams are measured on the outcomes they create for the business or customer, not the volume of activity or deliverables produced
principles.rationale: Output measures incentivise busy-work; outcome measures focus effort on what matters
implications: KPIs cascade from customer/business outcomes
Roadmaps include outcome hypotheses, not just deliverables
Quarterly reviews assess outcome attainment, not feature delivery

principles.name: Decide where the work happens
principles.statement: Decision authority lives with the team closest to the customer and the data
principles.rationale: Escalating routine decisions is slow and removes context; teams cannot be accountable for outcomes they cannot influence
implications: Decision rights are explicit per role/team
Escalation is for genuine cross-team conflict, not routine choices
Leaders coach decision-making rather than make decisions on others' behalf

principles.name: Continuous discovery over big design up front
principles.statement: Validate assumptions cheaply and continuously; do not commit to a multi-year plan ahead of evidence
principles.rationale: Markets, customer needs, and technology shift faster than long-cycle planning can absorb
implications: No initiative passes commitment without an evidence-based shaping phase
Discovery and delivery overlap; the team that learns also builds
Funding is staged against learning milestones, not Gantt milestones

principles.name: Customer journey as the unit of design
principles.statement: Business processes are designed end-to-end from the customer's point of view, not departmentally
principles.rationale: Customers experience the seams; internally optimised processes regularly produce externally poor outcomes
implications: Every core process has a named journey owner spanning departments
Internal SLAs are derived from the customer-facing promise, not vice versa
BUS-PRO entries reference the customer journey they serve

principles.name: Process digital by default
principles.statement: A new or redesigned business process is fully digital end-to-end unless a documented constraint requires manual steps
principles.rationale: Digital execution is faster, auditable, measurable, and the only basis for AI-assisted operations later
implications: Manual workarounds in core processes require a remediation plan
Process designs ship with the data model and event flow, not just the steps
Documents leaving the business are produced by systems, not authored by hand

principles.name: Sustainability is a line-management responsibility
principles.statement: Carbon, ESG, and social-impact metrics are owned by operating leaders alongside cost, quality, and safety
principles.rationale: Centralising sustainability creates a parallel reporting function disconnected from the work
implications: Operational KPI dashboards include sustainability metrics by default
Investment cases must state environmental impact
Sustainability sign-off is a line-management duty, not a separate gate
